Brahmavaivartapurāṇa
the 10th among the 18 Mahāpurāṇas; Composed after 8th Cent. a popular text of the Rādhākṛṣṇa Cult elevating Kṛṣṇa a. the Supreme God; divided into four parts (276 chs.)--Brahma (30 chs.). Prakṛti (67 chs.), Gaṇapati (46 chs.) an. Śri kṛṣṇajanma (133 chs.); total number of verses given a. 18000 in Matsyapurāṇa an. Nāradapurāṇa; the Kṛṣṇajanmakhaṇḍa ch. 132 gives a table of its contents; not q. by early nibandha writers; had undergone many changes; on the quotations from this Purāṇa in dh. texts but not found in the present Purāṇa text see R. C. Hazra, Studies in Puranic Records on Hindu Rites an. Customs p.. 166--67. [Page196-a.
